summary.intent: Continue the remaining work on the Callisto repo: make the preview paths resolve against --cwd, then add release-PR labels derived from the preview's findings.
summary.outcome: Opened PR #478 (preview paths resolve against --cwd, signed, description updated) and pushed feat/pr-labels with labels support (model report field, action script create/add/remove, contract and Rust tests, docs, changeset). The labels PR number was being looked up at the end; CI on the new commits was not run.

repo: main currently fails to compile its tests until #477 merges (a ChangelogInput test literal in release_preview.rs missing `style`); branches carry the identical one-line fix so their checks run independently and the hunk applies cleanly whichever merges first.
ComposePrBodyReport in callisto-model is a public, schema-generating wire type, so adding a field touches the wire contract and needs a model serialization test and docs.
Only --emit-decision (a committed repo file) stays workspace-root-relative; --emit-preview and compose-pr-body --preview now resolve against --cwd like other file flags (resolve_file_arg in cli.rs).

The release PR action's contract test (.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh) stubs gh; label creation is only asserted in the case where the label list stub says labels don't exist.

Commits are expected to be signed (checked via commit verification reason); PRs are linked with `entire trail link` and verified with `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` and workflow contract scripts.

code.finding: Test ChangelogInput literal lacks the `style` field, breaking test compilation on main; fixed by #477 and duplicated on the two new branches.
Previously handled a single label; extended to create missing managed labels, add applied ones and remove ones that stopped applying, without hardcoding names.
Holds ComposePrBodyReport; now lists each managed label with an applied flag.

workflow: Use all-or-nothing Python edit scripts run with `python3 -I` plus mutation checks to confirm tests actually catch regressions before committing.
When a change was made on the wrong branch, isolate it by cutting a new branch from main and moving the edits, keeping the original worktree clean.
Temporarily apply a pending fix locally to verify, then revert before committing, and later include it deliberately when CI independence is needed.
When an unfamiliar item (e.g. 'change 191/disinfectant', '86') appears, verify via gh/grep rather than guess.

friction: main was red due to the unmerged #477, forcing a local temporary patch for verification and later duplicating the fix in branches.
PR #478 CI failed for the same reason until the fix was added to it.
My first contract-test assertion for label creation was placed in the wrong case (labels stubbed as existing) and had to be corrected.
Label edits were initially made on the preview-paths branch and had to be moved to a separate branch.
